title: Let the Finger Pointing Begin!
summary: The effort to stop the gushing oil well 5,000 feet below sea level in the Gulf of Mexico has moved into a critical next stage with the arrival of a four‐story containment dome designed to capture the oil at the site. The 100‐ton concrete and steel dome is being guided by cameras as robots lower it directly above the well currently spewing oil into the U.S. The dome will then be connected to a vessel at the surface, which, if successful, officials hope will capture as much as 85% of the oil coming from the site by Sunday.

children.title: Managing Expectations
children.summary: Despite the expectations of many, the Deepwater Horizon spill has, to date, had only a moderate impact on freight rates in the tanker market. Specially‐crafted clauses have been inserted into charterparties for voyages through the area, as owners naturally seek a premium for taking the risks associated with bringing their vessels into the US Gulf.

children.title: Slowing Momentum
children.summary: The clearest indication of the spill's immediate impact is the 30‐day moratorium on new exploration licenses announced by President Obama almost immediately following the accident. It is highly likely that the spill will delay those efforts for far longer than 30 days as it will take years for all of the investigations likely to stem from the incident to run their course.

children.title: Undiscovered Resources
children.summary: Coming on the heels of a rhetorical embrace of the role of domestic oil and gas production in meeting America's long‐term energy goals by the Obama Administration, the Deepwater Horizon spill could not have come at a worse time for U.S. On the bright side for tanker owners nervously watching developments from the sidelines: it looks like we will continue to be import‐bound for at least the time being.
